paper_metadata.title: A Review of High-Temperature Toughness Improvement Strategies for Medium Entropy Alloys
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.section: 1. Introduction
evidence.quote: MEA refers to an alloy made by melting two to four elements with the same atomic ratio, and the structure entropy is between 1 and 1.5R. MEAs generally have a relatively simple crystal structure, low stacking fault energy (SFE) and some mechanical properties lacking in traditional alloys

evidence.section: 1. Introduction

evidence.section: 2. Effect of Phase Transformation Strengthening on Toughness of MEA
evidence.quote: Chung et al. (Ref 33) developed a series of two phase CoCrNiMox (x = 0.4, 0.6, 0.7, 0.83 and 1.0) MEAs with r phase and FCC phase, and their fracture behaviors were systematically studied. It was found that with the volume fraction of r phase increases from 4 to 72%, the fracture toughness ( KIc) of the two phase MEA decreases from 72 to 8 MPa * m0.5.

evidence.section: 2. Effect of Phase Transformation Strengthening on Toughness of MEA
evidence.quote: Lu et al. (Ref 15) studied the alloying effect of Al element on the structure and mechanical properties of CrCoNi MEA, and found that the yield strength of the MEAs after adding Al element can reach 1226 MPa, and the fracture strain is 21.97%.
